conviction_note: Small positive lean (p_up 56 on abs 5.5): Q2's lower cost base, run at last year's Q3/Q2 seasonal ratio, implies adjusted EPS near $0.29-0.30 against a $0.23-0.25 consensus, and October existing-home volumes (+20% yoy) plus the 1 Oct mortgage subsidy give the call a positive Q4 story. This runs against a +4.1 vol-point put skew and an unhelpful reaction record (beats bought +3% to +7%, a soft quarter sold), so p_up stays near 50. Revenue should come in roughly at the bar because renovation (-30%) and rental (-15%) are being shrunk on purpose. Findings sum +0.9, scaled +0.66; the two agree.

positioning_check: Short interest 22.8m shares, about 2.1% of shares outstanding, 6.08 days to cover (FINRA settlement 2026-10-30), down 25.6% from a 30.7m peak on 2026-10-15 (https://equibles.com/stocks/beke/shortinterest, read 2026-11-13). This is not a crowded short, and the shorts already covered into late October. Option skew: +4.09 vol points (25d put IV over call IV), so the market pays for downside. Put/call OI 0.65. Event-implied move 5.19% (straddle 6.33%, 7 days). Tape: -5.73% over 5 days and -1.66% over 20, 9% below the 52-week high; the stock gave back its post-Q2 breakout attempt ($18.85 on 2026-11-06, $17.77 now). Sentiment per the finviz preview moved from modestly bullish to slightly bearish. The company is buying back steadily (see findings).

findings.finding: Q3 2026 market data put existing-home transaction volume up about 7-9% yoy and prices down about 7%. China Index Academy's 20-city existing-home units: July +9.3% yoy (125k), Jan-Aug cumulative +6.3% (implying August around +7-8%), September +7.4% (119k); 100-city resale prices -7.08% yoy in August. In Q2 Beike's platform resale orders grew 25% against a 20-city market growing about 10%, and its existing-home GTV rose 8.0%. Against the Q3 2025 base of RMB505.6bn existing-home GTV and RMB5.99bn revenue, that supports existing-home GTV of roughly +3% to +10% and revenue on the line up low-to-mid single digits. That is broadly what a -5.8% total revenue consensus already assumes for transactions.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-21): existing-home GTV +8%, the first positive total GTV in a year, plus an EPS beat ($0.42 vs $0.31); the stock rose about 3% (https://www-web.itiger.com/news/1141424047). Q3 2025: existing GTV +5.8%, shares +7% premarket (https://www.itiger.com/news/2582824989).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. These are public monthly series, so if they were a surprise the revenue consensus would not sit at -5.8%. Beike's own outperformance of the market (+25% orders vs about +10%) is the unpriced part, and only if it persisted. Filed as a proxy, not a company number.
findings.independence: Proxy (industry series, not company data). Q2 company figures: https://finviz.com/news/384441/ke-holdings-inc-announces-second-quarter-2026-unaudited-financial-results. CRIC put September resale growth at only +3.1% yoy, a weaker read (same search, https://news.10jqka.com.cn/20261010/c680542868.shtml).

findings.finding: Peer read is softer. 5I5J (我爱我家), the listed Beijing-centric broker that reported on 2026-10-25, after Beike last spoke, posted Q3 brokerage GTV of RMB46.6bn, only +1.7% yoy, and Q3 revenue -3.96%. That is weaker than the 20-city volume series and is a sign that price declines are eating volume growth in GTV terms, the 'volume-price divergence' management flagged.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of BEKE reacting to 5I5J prints. BEKE's reaction to its own existing-home GTV line: +3% on Q2 2026 (+8% GTV).
findings.why_not_priced: A Shenzhen-listed A-share peer print gets little attention from US BEKE holders, and no BEKE preview found cites it. If it were priced, the previews would carry a lower existing-home GTV expectation than the Q2 +8%.
findings.independence: Different company, so independent of the CIA series in finding 1, which it partly offsets. Revenue figure: https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610253907259926.html. 5I5J is Beijing/Hangzhou-heavy, Beike is national, and Beike gained share in Q2, so the transmission is partial.

findings.finding: Profit run-rate looks above the EPS bar. Q2 2026 adjusted net income was RMB3,185m (adjusted EPS $0.42), with gross margin 28.6% (+6.7pt), adjusted operating margin 14.6% and GAAP opex down 14%. In 2025, Q3 adjusted net income (RMB1,286m) was 0.71x Q2's (RMB1,821m). Applied to Q2 2026 that gives about RMB2.25bn, or about $0.29-0.30 per ADS, against a $0.23-0.25 consensus (year-ago $0.16 adjusted) and a $0.30 whisper. The renovation contraction is 'basically complete' and margins rose in every segment. The downside: the CFO said not to extrapolate one quarter's profit, Q2 carried a RMB280m bad-debt provision on SINIC receivables that could recur, and new-home receivables risk persists.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 EPS beat ($0.42 vs $0.31) with margin at a 3-year high: about +3% (https://www-web.itiger.com/news/1141424047). Q1 2026: an EPS miss reported ($0.47 vs est.) with shares -2.9% (low-quality source, unverified). Q4 2025 (2026-03-16): shares slid (https://rallies.ai/news/ke-holdings-beke-falls-as-q4-results-and-china-housing-data-pressure-sentiment). Margin beats have been bought modestly, not strongly.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $0.25 implies Q3 adjusted net income of about RMB2.0bn, a 37% sequential drop, steeper than last year's 29% seasonal drop despite a structurally lower cost base. If the market priced the run-rate, consensus would sit at the $0.30 whisper and the stock would not have fallen 5.7% in the week before the print. The EPS bar is disputed ($0.21-$0.25), so the size is capped.
findings.independence: Inference from company primary documents (two 6-Ks), not a Q3 number. Tiger's preview carries EBIT +189% yoy to RMB2.59bn, which points the same way (https://www.itiger.com/news/1181708277). The finviz preview flags the SINIC provision risk against it (https://finviz.com/news/418743/ke-holdings-must-prove-its-margin-breakout-can-survive-a-softer-third-quarter).

findings.finding: Q4 commentary has a tailwind the call will be asked about. China Index Academy says 20-city existing-home units rose +20% yoy over 1-28 October (vs +7.4% in September), and 18 key cities rose +17.5% for the month. A 1-percentage-point first-home mortgage interest subsidy for new and resale homes took effect 1 October 2026. Resale makes up about 27% of qualifying first-tier transactions vs 7.8% for new homes, so it skews to Beike's existing-home business. New-home sales stayed weak (-13% in 30 cities).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BEKE gives no numeric guidance. At Q2 the qualitative 'the second quarter is not the end, but the beginning' plus the beat bought about +3%. No clean record of a reaction to Q4 commentary alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the data is public. But the stock fell 5.7% in the five sessions to 2026-11-13 and sits 9% under its high with puts bid, which is not what a market already pricing a strong-Q4 resale story looks like. Management confirming October-November platform volumes (company-level, not the 20-city proxy) is the unpriced part.
findings.independence: Proxy, macro-to-company. A second source on October: https://news.ifeng.com/c/8xmktEQP8O0 (18 cities +17.5%). Not confirmed by the company yet.

findings.finding: The new-home line is a drag. Beike's new-home revenue (RMB6.64bn in Q3 2025, about 29% of revenue) faces a weak market: 100-city new-home sales -7% yoy in August, 30-city new-home area -13% in October, and an 28 August policy package that pushes presale toward completed-home sales and hit developer stocks (HK developers index -6.2%). Beike's Q2 new-home GTV was only +1.2% with resources concentrated on premium projects. Net of the rest: existing-home and rental margins are rising, so this hits revenue more than profit (new-home contribution margin 28.8%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: new-home GTV -13.7% and revenue -14.1%, yet the stock rose about 7% premarket on margins/buyback. This name has looked through new-home weakness before.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: consensus revenue already falls 5.8%. The residual is that new-home GTV could print negative again against a +1.2% Q2, which previews do not highlight (the finviz preview mentions only 'new-home demand weakening').
findings.independence: Proxy (industry series). The finviz preview independently flags weakening new-home demand: https://finviz.com/news/418743/ke-holdings-must-prove-its-margin-breakout-can-survive-a-softer-third-quarter. The reaction history says this line has been looked through.

findings.finding: Buybacks are steady. The company bought 11.51m Class A shares (about 3.8m ADS, around $65-70m at $5.49-6.23 a share) in 25 tranches between 1 October and 4 November 2026, and cut its share count by 19.22m in October, roughly matching the Q2 pace of about $250m a quarter. About $2.0bn remains on the $5bn authorization to August 2028. Repurchases in the current period are likely to be quoted on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025's record $281m repurchase came with a +7% premarket move (https://www.itiger.com/news/2582824989), alongside margins.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the buybacks are disclosed daily on HKEX. Only an acceleration or a new authorization would be news, and I found no sign of one.
findings.independence: Share-count reduction disclosed in a separate HKEX monthly return: https://www.itiger.com/news/1191510753.
